subject: emergency-management
intro: Emergency management leads to the coordination professions: directors who run the cycle for counties and companies, logisticians who move supplies into disasters, inspectors who cut hazards before they ignite, and safety specialists protecting workplaces.

roles.title: Emergency Management Directors
roles.what: Prepare plans and procedures for responding to catastrophes: coordinate disaster response, run training and exercises, apply for federal recovery funds, and direct operations when an emergency strikes the community or organisation.
roles.where: This course is the job description — the mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery cycle, NIMS and the Incident Command System, emergency operations plans, exercises and after-action reviews, and disaster declarations.

roles.title: Logisticians
roles.what: Analyse and coordinate an organisation's supply chains: forecast needs, manage procurement and inventory, and direct the movement of goods and people — including the surge of relief supplies after a disaster.
roles.where: Multi-agency coordination in the NIMS and ICS unit is essentially logistics under pressure, and the resource staging you study in preparedness planning is the discipline this career formalises.

roles.title: Fire Inspectors and Investigators
roles.what: Inspect buildings for fire hazards and enforce fire codes, and investigate fires and explosions to determine their origin and cause, documenting findings that prevent the next disaster.
roles.where: Hazard identification and analysis from the risk assessment unit trains the inspection mindset, and the codes and standards awareness you build in mitigation projects matches fire code enforcement work.

roles.title: Occupational Health and Safety Specialists
roles.what: Inspect workplaces, collect and test samples, and analyse hazards that could harm workers, designing procedures and training that keep operations safe and compliant with health and safety regulations.
roles.where: Risk mapping and hazard analysis, public warning and communication, and the exercises and after-action review topics are the core methods of workplace safety programmes this career runs.
